payload.markdown: This pattern is very useful, but there are a few issues to be aware of. You need to be sure that all modify operations actually do mark the object in question as dirty. Failing to do this can result in hard-to-spot bugs. You may like to look at other ways of testing for modified objects. Reflection sounds like a good option there, but you should look into the performance implications of such testing—the pattern is meant to improve efficiency, not undermine it.

items: Reflection: Inspecting classes, methods and properties from running code.
Classes & Objects: A class defines state and behaviour; objects are instances of that definition.
Factory Pattern: Creating objects through a dedicated creator instead of new at every call site.
Object Identity: === compares instance identity: two objects with equal fields are still distinct.
Pattern Principles: What design patterns are, how to describe them, and when one fits.
Strategy Pattern: Swapping an algorithm behind a common interface at runtime.
Unit of Work: Tracking changes to many objects and writing them in a single transaction.
